extracted.intended_audience: B2B PR professionals, startup founders, marketing and communications leaders at enterprise-focused tech companies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting, quoting, and distributing B2B press releases and stories aimed at driving enterprise buyer interest, analyst recognition, talent recruitment, and investor confidence. Emphasizes data-driven story types, quote standards, and a specific distribution mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inbound demo requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize B2B PR to drive inbound demo requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat inbound demo requests as a primary success metric rather than vanity metrics or impressions; set up tracking to measure demo requests generated from PR activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enterprise buyer awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: PR should increase awareness among enterprise buyers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target messaging, outlets, and timing to reach decision-makers at enterprise accounts rather than broad consumer audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyst recognition (Gartner, Forrester quadrants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PR to gain recognition from industry analysts (e.g., Gartner, Forrester).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize analyst briefings and positioning that supports analyst inclusion in reports/quadrants; brief analysts before public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talent recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PR to help recruit talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position product/technical narrative in ways that attract engineers and other hires (technical detail in stories can help).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PR to build investor confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include investor-facing signals such as measurable customer outcomes, clear use-of-funds in funding announcements, and thoughtful investor quotes (reasoning, not cheerleading).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do NOT optimize for consumer-style impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid treating consumer-style reach/impressions as a primary objective for B2B PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B2B success metrics differ from consumer metrics; focus on channels and messages that influence buying committees, not mass impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do NOT optimize for vanity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid optimizing for vanity metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vanity metrics (e.g., raw impressions, social likes) are insufficient — track inbound/demo metrics and meaningful engagement instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do NOT optimize for general brand awareness in irrelevant audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not aim PR at irrelevant audiences just to boost brand awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure audiences reached are relevant to enterprise sales, analysts, talent, or investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do NOT optimize for social media virality
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid chasing social media virality as an objective for B2B PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virality can attract irrelevant attention; prioritize targeted reach and credibility with buyers and analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Win Story — required components
rubrics_metrics.description: A Customer Win Story should include a named enterprise customer, a measurable outcome, and technical detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a real enterprise customer name, present concrete metrics (e.g., % improvement, $ saved), and include technical specifics that explain how the outcome was achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry Data Report — required components
rubrics_metrics.description: An Industry Data Report should use proprietary platform data, include segmented insights, and present benchmark comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose methodology and sample size; ensure N is large enough and segments/benchmarks are meaningful. Avoid releasing survey data with too-small N or missing methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards/Category Definition — required components
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a Standards/Category Definition by naming a new category, defining its rules, and positioning your company as the leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear definitions and rules for the category and show why your company sets the standards; use evidence and framing to justify leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO/CTO quote standards
rubrics_metrics.description: CEO/CTO quotes should reference specific technical or market reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid generic platitudes; quotes from executives should add factual, technical, or market context that supports the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer quote standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer quotes should include numbers (e.g., % improvement, $ saved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes need concrete metrics to be credible and useful for buyers and analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyst quote guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid analyst quotes unless they're free of paid relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyst quotes are acceptable only if there is no paid relationship that could create perceived bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor quote guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Investor quotes should be reasoning, not cheerleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investor quotes must explain why they believe in the company or its market rather than offering generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology disclosure for any data
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose methodology for any data used in PR (sample size, segmentation, how data was collected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about survey/sample size and methods; anti-patterns include releasing survey data with N too small or omitting methodology altogether.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution mix and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a specific distribution mix and timing: trade press first, analyst briefings before public release, LinkedIn newsletter same day, wire for SEO, and webinar/podcast the week of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended order: trade press (InformationWeek, TechCrunch Enterprise, ZDNet) → analyst briefings prior to public release → publish LinkedIn newsletter same day → wire distribution for SEO (because B2B buyers Google before buying) → webinar/podcast appearances during the week of release. Coordinate timing so analysts and targeted press are briefed before public announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic 'AI-powered' claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make generic 'AI-powered' claims without specifics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generic AI claims are a common failure; provide technical detail and concrete outcomes instead of buzzwords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid nonspecific customer quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer quotes that say nothing specific are failure modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure customer quotes provide concrete metrics or specifics; otherwise they add no credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcements must include use-of-funds clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding announcements should state how funds will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A funding announcement without use-of-funds clarity is a common PR failure and misses an opportunity to tell a strategic story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publishing survey data with insufficient N or missing methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey-based stories must have adequate sample size and disclosed methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If N is too small or methodology is missing, the data will be treated as low-quality and can harm credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague platform benefit statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid statements like 'Our platform helps companies...' without specifying what kind of companies or results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about who benefits and how; vague benefit claims fail to inform buyers or analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure inbound metrics, not just impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Track inbound/demo metrics (leads, demo requests) rather than impressions alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up analytics to attribute inbound actions to PR channels; use these outcomes to evaluate PR effectiveness instead of relying on superficial metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story type should match B2B repertoire
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick story types that work in B2B (customer wins, data reports, category definitions) rather than consumer story formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the chosen story aligns with enterprise buyer needs, includes technical detail and measurable outcomes, and fits the distribution plan.
